title: Abraham waited twenty-five years for Isaac.
paragraphs: Abraham waited twenty-five years for Isaac.
Think about that for a moment.

Twenty-five years of prayers.
Twenty-five years of hoping.
Twenty-five years of believing a promise that seemed impossible.

God had told Abraham that his descendants would become a great nation. Yet year after year passed with no child. His body grew older. Sarah’s womb remained barren. The promise looked more and more unrealistic.
But eventually, the miracle came.
Isaac was born.

He wasn’t just a son.
He was the living proof that God keeps His word.
Every laugh Isaac made must have reminded Abraham of the faithfulness of God. Every step the boy took must have felt like watching the future unfold. Isaac carried the promise of generations.
And then one day, everything changed.
In Genesis 22, God said something that must have shaken Abraham to the core:
“Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love… and offer him as a burnt offering.”
Imagine hearing those words.

The very son God had promised…
The very miracle Abraham waited decades for…
Now God was asking for him back.
The Bible tells us plainly what this moment was:
“God tested Abraham.” (Genesis 22:1)

This was not cruelty.
This was not confusion.
This was a test of faith.
Because sometimes the greatest test of faith is not believing God for a miracle.
Sometimes the greatest test is trusting God with the miracle after it arrives.
Isaac had become Abraham’s joy. His hope. His future.
But God was revealing something deeper.

Would Abraham trust the gift…
or the Giver?
Early the next morning, Abraham set out for Mount Moriah.
Notice something remarkable.
Scripture records no argument.

No delay.
No negotiation.
No attempt to rewrite God’s command.
Abraham simply obeyed.
Can you imagine the three-day journey to the mountain?

Three days walking beside the son he loved.
Three days hearing Isaac’s voice.
Three days knowing what waited at the end of the road.
Yet Abraham continued forward.
Why?
Because his faith had reached a level many people miss.
The book of Hebrews gives us insight into Abraham’s thinking:
“Abraham reasoned that God could even raise the dead.” (Hebrews 11:19)
Think about that.
Abraham believed something radical.

Even if Isaac died…
God would still keep His promise.
In other words, Abraham trusted God beyond logic, beyond explanation, and beyond visible outcomes.
This is what mature faith looks like.
Faith does not say, “I understand everything.”
Faith says, “I trust God even when I don’t.”
When they reached the mountain, Isaac asked a haunting question:
“The fire and the wood are here… but where is the lamb for the offering?”
Abraham replied with words that echo through history:
“God Himself will provide the lamb.” (Genesis 22:8)
Those words carried more truth than Abraham may have even realized.
Because as Abraham raised the knife, an angel stopped him.
“Do not lay a hand on the boy.”
At that moment, God provided a ram caught in a thicket to take Isaac’s place.
The sacrifice was stopped.
Isaac lived.
But the story was never only about Abraham and Isaac.
This moment was also a prophetic shadow.
Mount Moriah sits in the same region where centuries later another sacrifice would happen.
But this time, the Son would not be spared.
God would give His own Son, Jesus Christ, for the salvation of the world.

The Son Abraham did not have to lose…
points forward to the Son God chose to give.
And suddenly the story becomes even more powerful.
Because Abraham was asked to do what God Himself would one day actually do.
This story teaches us something that still challenges believers today.
Faith is not proven when everything is comfortable.
Faith is proven when we place what we love most back into God’s hands.
Sometimes the greatest idols in our lives are not evil things.
They are good things we hold too tightly.

A dream.
A relationship.
A career.
A future we imagined.

But true faith trusts that God is still good…
even when we surrender the things we cherish most.
Abraham discovered something profound on that mountain.
When you trust God fully, He always provides.

Sometimes He provides a miracle.
Sometimes He provides a ram in the thicket.
But He always provides what is needed to fulfill His purpose.
And that leaves us with a deeply personal question.
If God asked you to place the thing you love most on the altar…
Would you trust Him with it?
Because the greatest faith is not just believing God for blessings.
The greatest faith is believing that God Himself is enough.
“Now I know that you fear God,” the angel said, “because you have not withheld your son, your only son, from Me.” (Genesis 22:12)
Abraham went up the mountain with a test.
He came down with a deeper revelation:
God is faithful, even when faith costs everything.
So let me ask you something honestly.
What is the “Isaac” in your life right now?
And could you trust God with it?
